description: Saving, continuing, a best score kept between runs, and translations

examples.intent: Continue from where you left off

input.natural_language: A title screen with New game and Continue (only when there is a save); every room saves on entry, and the best score is kept between runs

expected_output.quantum_code:
<q:application id="saves" type="game">
  <q:set name="score" value="0" type="number" />
  <q:set name="best" value="0" type="number" saved="true" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />

  <qg:scene name="title" width="270" height="144">
    <qg:menu>
      <qg:button label="New game">
        <q:set name="score" value="0" />
        <qg:goto-scene name="room-1" />
      </qg:button>
      <qg:button label="Continue" if="{has_save()}"><qg:continue /></qg:button>
    </qg:menu>
    <qg:hud position="bottom-center"><qg:counter bind="best" label="BEST " /></qg:hud>
  </qg:scene>

  <qg:scene name="room-1" width="270" height="144" save="true">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="topdown" sheet="chars" frame="0" x="40" y="72" hitbox="14x14" />
    <qg:on-input action="jump">
      <q:set name="score" value="{score + 1}" />
      <q:set name="best" value="{max(best, score)}" />
    </qg:on-input>
    <qg:on-input action="select">
      <qg:save scene="room-2" />
      <qg:goto-scene name="room-2" />
    </qg:on-input>
  </qg:scene>

  <qg:scene name="room-2" width="270" height="144" save="true">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="topdown" sheet="chars" frame="0" x="40" y="72" hitbox="14x14" />
    <qg:on-input action="cancel"><qg:goto-scene name="title" /></qg:on-input>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>
expected_output.runtime_behavior: Entering a room with save="true" saves the game state and that room. Continue shows only when has_save() is true and brings the game state back and goes to the saved room. best has saved="true": it is kept between runs even without a save.

examples.intent: The game in Portuguese and Spanish

input.natural_language: Translate the game's texts to Portuguese and Spanish, with a menu button that switches the language

expected_output.quantum_code:
<q:application id="langs" type="game">
  <q:set name="coins" value="0" type="number" />
  <qg:spritesheet name="chars" src="assets/kenney/tilemap-characters_packed.png" tile="24" />
  <qg:language lang="pt" name="Português">
    <qg:phrase text="Play" as="Jogar" />
    <qg:phrase text="Language" as="Idioma" />
    <qg:phrase text="COINS" as="MOEDAS" />
    <qg:phrase text="Hello!" as="Olá!" />
  </qg:language>
  <qg:language lang="es" name="Español">
    <qg:phrase text="Play" as="Jugar" />
    <qg:phrase text="Language" as="Idioma" />
    <qg:phrase text="COINS" as="MONEDAS" />
    <qg:phrase text="Hello!" as="¡Hola!" />
  </qg:language>

  <qg:scene name="title" width="270" height="144">
    <qg:menu>
      <qg:button label="Play"><qg:goto-scene name="main" /></qg:button>
      <qg:button label="{tr('Language') + ': ' + language()}"><qg:next-language /></qg:button>
    </qg:menu>
  </qg:scene>

  <qg:scene name="main" width="270" height="144">
    <qg:character id="hero" controller="topdown" sheet="chars" frame="0" x="40" y="72" hitbox="14x14" />
    <qg:hud>
      <qg:counter bind="coins" label="COINS" />
      <qg:text value="{tr('Hello!')}" />
    </qg:hud>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>
expected_output.runtime_behavior: Texts written in the game (a button's label, a counter's label) are shown in the player's language when a phrase gives them; tr() translates a text an expression puts together. The language button cycles English, Português, Español and the choice is kept for the next run.

examples.intent: The version always in view, and a link to what is new

input.natural_language: A title screen that shows the game's version in a corner, as every screen does, and a button that opens the changelog page in the browser, in the player's language

expected_output.quantum_code:
<q:application id="news" type="game">
  <qg:language lang="pt" name="Português">
    <qg:phrase text="What's new" as="Novidades" />
  </qg:language>
  <q:function name="game_version"><q:return value="{'2.0'}" /></q:function>
  <qg:scene name="title" width="320" height="180">
    <qg:hud position="bottom-right">
      <qg:text value="{'v' + game_version()}" />
    </qg:hud>
    <qg:menu>
      <qg:button label="Play"><qg:goto-scene name="main" /></qg:button>
      <qg:button label="{tr('What\'s new') + ' (v' + game_version() + ')'}">
        <qg:open-url href="{'https://example.com/game/changelog/' + ('pt/' if language() == 'Português' else '')}" />
      </qg:button>
    </qg:menu>
  </qg:scene>
  <qg:scene name="main" width="320" height="180">
    <qg:hud position="bottom-right"><qg:text value="{'v' + game_version()}" /></qg:hud>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>
expected_output.runtime_behavior: The version is a function, not the state: a save of an older version does not bring its number back. The button opens the changelog in a new tab in a browser, in the system's browser elsewhere; played by an agent it opens nothing and the "open-url" event says the address.

examples.intent: A bug report from inside the game, with what it was doing

input.natural_language: Buttons that open the game's report form in the browser, already filled in with the kind of report and where the player was (the version, the world, the club, the language), so a player only writes what happened

expected_output.quantum_code:
<q:application id="report" type="game">
  <q:set name="world" value="7" type="number" />
  <q:set name="club" value="Onça Pintada" type="string" />
  <q:function name="report_url" params="kind">
    <q:return value="{'https://example.com/forms/report?kind=' + url_encode(kind) + '&context=' + url_encode('v1.0; world ' + str(world) + '; ' + club + '; ' + language())}" />
  </q:function>
  <qg:scene name="title" width="320" height="180">
    <qg:menu>
      <qg:button label="Report a bug"><qg:open-url href="{report_url('Bug')}" /></qg:button>
      <qg:button label="Suggest something"><qg:open-url href="{report_url('Sugestão')}" /></qg:button>
    </qg:menu>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>
expected_output.runtime_behavior: url_encode() writes each text as a part of the address (a space as %20, the ç of Onça as %C3%A7, an & as %26), so the form receives it whole. The button opens the form in a new tab in a browser, in the system's browser elsewhere; played by an agent it opens nothing and the "open-url" event says the address.

examples.intent: A beta's report, from any screen, to a server

input.natural_language: A [!] on every screen, and F9, that opens a report panel over the screen being played: a bug or a suggestion, what happened, and Send, which posts it with where the player was and the saved game to the beta's server and says the number it got

expected_output.quantum_code:
<q:application id="beta" type="game">
  <q:set name="outbox" value="[]" type="array" saved="true" />
  <q:function name="game_version"><q:return value="{'2.1'}" /></q:function>
  <qg:input action="report" keys="F9" />
  <qg:touch-button action="report" x="308" y="12" size="16" label="!" show="always" />

  <qg:overlay name="report" action="report" shade="0.6">
    <q:set name="kind" value="bug" type="string" />
    <q:set name="text" value="" type="string" />
    <q:set name="seen" value="{scene_name()}" type="string" />
    <q:set name="option" value="{focused()}" type="string" />
    <q:set name="status" value="" type="string" />
    <qg:hud position="top-left">
      <qg:text value="{'Report from ' + seen + (' (' + option + ')' if option != '' else '')}" />
      <qg:text bind="status" />
    </qg:hud>
    <qg:menu y="60" x="40">
      <qg:button label="{'Kind: ' + kind}">
        <q:set name="kind" value="{'suggestion' if kind == 'bug' else 'bug'}" />
      </qg:button>
      <qg:field bind="text" label="What happened" max-length="400" />
      <qg:button label="Send">
        <q:set name="status" value="Sending" />
        <qg:post to="https://reports.example.com/api/reports"
                 data="{ {'game': 'beta', 'version': game_version(), 'kind': kind, 'text': text, 'screen': seen, 'option': option, 'save': save_text()} }">
          <qg:on-done><q:set name="status" value="{'Report no. ' + str(reply.number) + ' sent, thank you'}" /></qg:on-done>
          <qg:on-fail><q:set name="status" value="{'Not sent (' + reason + ')'}" /></qg:on-fail>
        </qg:post>
      </qg:button>
      <qg:button label="Back"><qg:close-overlay /></qg:button>
    </qg:menu>
  </qg:overlay>

  <qg:scene name="title" width="320" height="180">
    <qg:menu>
      <qg:button label="Play"><qg:goto-scene name="main" /></qg:button>
      <qg:button label="Report a bug or suggest"><qg:open-overlay name="report" /></qg:button>
    </qg:menu>
  </qg:scene>
  <qg:scene name="main" width="320" height="180">
    <qg:hud position="bottom-right"><qg:text value="{'v' + game_version() + ' beta'}" /></qg:hud>
  </qg:scene>
</q:application>
expected_output.runtime_behavior: The panel opens over whatever scene is shown, which stands still under it; scene_name() and focused() there are that scene and the option its cursor was on, save_text() the game as a save writes it. The report goes as JSON and the game goes on: the server's answer, or why it did not get through, comes a few ticks later. Back closes the panel and the scene goes on where it was.
